title: Comparing: más que, tan como, el mejor
summary: Compare and rank: más caro que, tan alto como, mejor, el más grande de, riquísimo.
focus: Comparatives of inequality and equality, irregular comparatives, and superlatives
content:
## More and less: más / menos … que

To compare two things, wrap the adjective (or adverb, or noun) in **más … que** (more … than) or **menos … que** (less … than). The adjective still agrees with the first noun.

- **Madrid es más grande que Toledo.** (Madrid is bigger than Toledo.)
- **Este piso es menos caro que el otro.** (This flat is less expensive than the other one.)
- **Ana corre más rápido que yo.** (Ana runs faster than me.)
- **Tengo más trabajo que tú.** (I have more work than you.)

Before a **number**, *than* is **de**, not *que*:

- **Cuesta más de cien euros.** (It costs more than a hundred euros.)
- **Tiene menos de veinte años.** (She is under twenty.)

## As … as: tan … como, tanto … como

Equality uses **como**. The first word depends on what you compare.

| before | use | example |
|---|---|---|
| an adjective or adverb | **tan … como** | **Soy tan alta como mi madre.** (I'm as tall as my mother.) |
| a noun | **tanto / tanta / tantos / tantas … como** | **Tengo tantos libros como tú.** (I have as many books as you.) |
| a verb (after it) | **tanto como** | **Trabaja tanto como yo.** (He works as much as I do.) |

**Tanto** agrees with the noun: **tanta paciencia**, **tantas amigas**. **Tan** never changes.

Negatives work too: **No es tan difícil como parece.** (It's not as hard as it seems.)

## Four irregulars: mejor, peor, mayor, menor

Four adjectives have a one-word comparative. Never say *más bueno* or *más grande* for these meanings.

| adjective | comparative | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| bueno | **mejor** | better |
| malo | **peor** | worse |
| grande (age) | **mayor** | older |
| pequeño (age) | **menor** | younger |

- **Este restaurante es mejor que ese.** (This restaurant is better than that one.)
- **Mi hermano es mayor que yo.** (My brother is older than me.)

The plurals are **mejores**, **peores**, **mayores**, **menores**. For physical size, **más grande / más pequeño** is normal, as in **Mi coche es más grande que el tuyo.** The adverbs are the same words, as in **cocinas mejor que yo** (you cook better than me).

## The best of all: superlatives and -ísimo

The superlative is the comparative with the article in front. The group it applies to is introduced by **de**:

- **Es el hotel más caro de la ciudad.** (It's the most expensive hotel in the city.)
- **Son las playas más bonitas de España.** (They're the prettiest beaches in Spain.)
- **Lucía es la mejor de la clase.** (Lucía is the best in the class.)

The noun can stay or go: **el hotel más caro** or **el más caro**.

For "extremely", drop the final vowel and add **-ísimo / -a / -os / -as**: **grandísimo**, **facilísimo**, **La paella está riquísima.** Watch the spelling. The letter **c** becomes **qu** (rico gives **riquísimo**), **g** becomes **gu** (largo gives **larguísimo**), and the word loses its old accent (difícil gives **dificilísimo**).

quiz.explanation: A comparison of inequality is más + adjective + que: 'más grande que'. 'De' only appears before numbers or in superlatives.
For age, 'older' is the irregular comparative mayor, not más grande.
hints: One of the four irregular comparatives: the one for age.

quiz.prompt: Este coche es tan rápido ___ el tuyo.
quiz.explanation: Equality uses tan … como: 'tan rápido como'. 'Que' goes with más/menos.
hints: Tan pairs with como, never que.

quiz.explanation: Before a noun, use tanto agreeing with it. Libros is masculine plural, so it is 'tantos libros como'.
hints: Tanto/a/os/as before a noun; tan before an adjective.

quiz.prompt: Which sentence compares the two restaurants correctly?
options: Este restaurante es mejor que ese.
Este restaurante es más bueno que ese.
Este restaurante es más mejor que ese.
quiz.correct_answer: Este restaurante es mejor que ese.
quiz.explanation: Bueno has the one-word comparative mejor, and you never add más to it.

quiz.prompt: Es el hotel más caro ___ la ciudad.
quiz.explanation: A superlative names its group with de: 'el más caro de la ciudad'. Que would turn it into a comparison with 'the city'.
hints: A superlative names its group with a small preposition.

quiz.prompt: Este móvil es barato: cuesta menos ___ cien euros.
quiz.explanation: Before a number, más/menos take de: 'menos de cien euros'.

quiz.prompt: Make it extreme: La paella está ___ (rico + -ísimo).
quiz.explanation: Drop the final -o, add -ísima to agree with paella, and spell c as qu before i: 'riquísima'.
hints: The c becomes qu before the i.

quiz.prompt: Este examen es ___ que el anterior. (worse)
quiz.explanation: Malo has the irregular comparative peor. Examen is singular, so it is not peores.

listening.meaning: It costs less than ten euros.
listening.note: Before a number, than is de, not que.

listening.text: Mi hermana es menor que yo.
listening.meaning: My sister is younger than me.

listening.text: Hoy hace más frío que ayer.
listening.meaning: It is colder today than yesterday.

listening.text: Carlos tiene tantos amigos como su hermano.
listening.meaning: Carlos has as many friends as his brother.
listening.note: Before a noun, tanto agrees: tantos amigos.

listening.text: Mi perro es tan rápido como el tuyo.
listening.meaning: My dog is as fast as yours.
listening.note: New word: el perro = the dog.

listening.text: Mi abuelo es el mayor de la familia.
listening.meaning: My grandfather is the oldest in the family.
listening.note: A superlative introduces its group with de.

listening.text: Esta tienda es más barata que la del centro.
listening.meaning: This shop is cheaper than the one in the centre.
listening.note: New word: la tienda = the shop.

listening.text: La sopa de mi abuela está riquísima, mejor que la del restaurante.
listening.meaning: My grandmother's soup is delicious, better than the restaurant's.

guide.tip: Three small words do most of the work: que after más/menos, como after tan/tanto, and de before a number or after a superlative.

conversations.title: Which flat?
conversations.scenario: Sara and Pablo have seen two flats and are deciding which one to rent.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: So, which flat do you like more?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: El de la calle Mayor es más grande que el otro, pero también es más caro.
lines.meaning: The one on Calle Mayor is bigger than the other one, but it's also more expensive.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí, cuesta más de novecientos euros al mes. Es carísimo.
lines.meaning: Yes, it costs more than nine hundred euros a month. It's really expensive.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: El pequeño es más barato, y está tan cerca del metro como el grande.
lines.meaning: The small one is cheaper, and it's as close to the metro as the big one.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Pero tiene menos luz que el otro. La cocina es peor.
lines.meaning: But it has less light than the other one. The kitchen is worse.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Es verdad. Aunque el barrio es mejor: es el más tranquilo de la ciudad.
lines.meaning: True. Although the neighbourhood is better: it's the quietest in the city.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿Y los vecinos? En el grande viven tantos estudiantes como en una residencia.
lines.meaning: And the neighbours? In the big one there are as many students as in a hall of residence.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Ja! Entonces el pequeño. Es menos bonito, pero mucho más tranquilo.
lines.meaning: Ha! The small one, then. It's less pretty, but much quieter.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Vale. Es la decisión más fácil del mundo.
lines.meaning: OK. It's the easiest decision in the world.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Facilísima. Llamo al dueño ahora mismo.
lines.meaning: Extremely easy. I'll call the owner right now.

bites.title: más … que
bites.rule: For more or less than, use más/menos + adjective + que. Before a number, use de instead of que: más de cien euros.
bites.example: Madrid es más grande que Toledo.

bites.title: tan … como
bites.rule: For as … as, use tan + adjective + como. Before a noun, use tanto/a/os/as, agreeing with it: tantos libros como tú.
bites.example: Soy tan alta como mi madre.
bites.example_meaning: I'm as tall as my mother.

bites.title: Four one-word comparatives
bites.rule: Bueno becomes mejor and malo becomes peor. For age, grande becomes mayor and pequeño becomes menor. Never say más bueno or más mejor.
bites.example: Mi hermano es mayor que yo.
bites.example_meaning: My brother is older than me.

bites.title: The most … of
bites.rule: A superlative is el/la/los/las + más/menos + adjective + de (the group). For 'extremely', add -ísimo: riquísimo, facilísimo.
bites.example: Es el hotel más caro de la ciudad.
bites.example_meaning: It's the most expensive hotel in the city.

sorts.title: que, como or de?
sorts.why: Use que after más/menos, como after tan/tanto, and de before a number or after a superlative.

sorts.title: How do you say 'more …'?
sorts.why: Only bueno, malo and grande/pequeño (for age) have one-word comparatives. Every other adjective takes más.

sorts.title: tan or tanto?
sorts.why: Tan goes before an adjective or adverb and never changes. Tanto goes before a noun and agrees with it.

spots.sentence: Madrid es más grande de Toledo.
spots.why: Más + adjective takes que. De is only for numbers and superlatives.

spots.sentence: Es el hotel más caro que la ciudad.
spots.why: A superlative introduces its group with de: el más caro de la ciudad.

spots.sentence: Soy tan alto que mi padre.

spots.why: Before a noun, tanto agrees: amigas is feminine plural.
Before a number, more than is más de.
Rico keeps its hard c sound before i by changing c to qu, giving riquísima.
